questions.question: Research shows that most riders in crashes:

options.text: Do not brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
Brake the front tire too much and do not brake the rear tire enough.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes do not use enough front brake and use too much rear brake.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear.
Use the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together whenever you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Move onto the shoulder.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: The center of your lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle can cause a collision. Riding on the far side can make the driver cut back into your lane too soon, which is also unsafe.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: You are passing another vehicle.
You need to slow down quickly.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your turn signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to slow down quickly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are not as visible as car brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice when you are slowing down faster than expected.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Give you an escape route.
Help you avoid wind from other vehicles.
Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should protect you from wind, other vehicles' blind spots, and road hazards. It should also discourage others from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: As weight moves to the front of your bike while braking, you should:

options.text: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Not worry about weight transfer—it has no effect.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: As the bike's weight moves forward during braking, slowly increase the pressure you apply to the front brake lever.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have rounded, or convex, mirrors. These mirrors:

options.text: Are easy to adjust to right away.
Make cars look closer than they really are.
Show a narrow view of the road.
Make cars look farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors, but they make objects appear farther away. You need to practice judging distances with convex mirrors if you are not used to them.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Needed even if you wear a helmet.
Only needed on windy days.
Not needed if you have a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed even if you wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection keeps you safe while letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear wheel while braking on a surface with good grip, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and shift down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear brake locks on a surface with good grip, keep it locked until you fully stop. Your motorcycle can still be controlled if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: How can you prevent another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Swerve side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast the alcohol is consumed
The drinker's body weight
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is the best protection when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.
Wear a good leather jacket.
Wear sturdy boots.
Know motorcycle laws well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Distance is your best protection against crashes. More space gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes. Proper gear is also important, but distance is your first defense.

questions.question: What is true about the center of a lane?

options.text: It is always the best place for a motorcycle to ride.
It often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
It often has oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
It is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of lanes. This area is usually safe to ride on unless the road is wet. Avoid large buildup of oil, which you may find at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: What should you do when going through a curve?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane through the entire curve.
Always stay in the left part of the lane through the entire curve.
Always stay in the right part of the lane through the entire curve.
Know that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to change your position in the lane at any time. The best path through a curve may not follow the road's curve.

questions.question: Which of the following should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen
Avoid other drivers' blind spots
Avoid surface hazards
Block your escape route

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots, avoids hazards, and discourages other drivers from sharing your lane. It should always give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other
Do both at the same time
Always brake first, then swerve
Use only the brakes instead

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other
questions.explanation: Do braking and swerving as separate actions. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: Why is it important to ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass?

options.text: The right side could be slippery
It helps you spot hazards in the next lane
People don't expect to be passed on their left
It puts you in the car's rearview mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you spot hazards in the next lane
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of your lane improves your view ahead. It makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What happens when you brake in a curve?

options.text: Use only the front brake
It is the same as braking on a straight road
You have more traction as you lean
You may have less traction as you lean

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When leaning into a curve, some tire traction is already used for turning. This means less traction is available for stopping.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes
Press hard on the front brake to prevent the tire from locking
Use only the rear brake
Use one brake at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Follow me
Slow down
Speed up
Exit

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals are used to communicate when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually more powerful than car headlights.
Usually just as powerful as car headlights.
Usually less powerful than car headlights.
Usually larger than car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually less powerful than car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Eight times
Ten times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive head injuries in a crash at any speed.

questions.question: When riding at night you should:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Decrease your following distance.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Wear tinted glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

options.text: Three times
Four times
Five times
Six times

questions.correctAnswerText: Five times
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: To be effective, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Prevent air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.
Restrict your side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses if needed.
